decisions.reason: The cited scaled bump can have support radius R>1, so the original supremum over |s|≤epsilon need not bound the integral. Fixed R with supp eta contained in [-R,R] gives the valid R epsilon bound; translation continuity still proves the full unchanged conclusion.

The Statement and Given explicitly require a real Hilbert space. Bilinearity and symmetry give the displayed square expansion exactly; a complex counterexample violates the hypotheses. The general descriptive title creates no complex assertion.

The actual published form Definition defines boundedness, coercivity and symmetry separately and expressly permits nonsymmetric real bilinear forms. The algorithm supplies common a.e. constants, finite-dimensional averaged coercive solves and exact reconstructions; symmetry is unnecessary.

Countable Choice is already a global hypothesis, so Riesz and Lax–Milgram apply to the real Hilbert space and both coercive transposed forms. F3 and A1 omitted the Riesz supplier assumption; both now state it accurately. Dense dual approximants and finite Galerkin inverse limits prove the claimed strong measurability and bounds without symmetry.

ACω cannot justify the originally asserted arbitrary dependent nested choices. Replaced step 1.1 by a unique left-first dyadic-half and least-index extraction for any bounded coordinate sequence; recursive application is deterministic and diagonal tails converge in every coordinate. Bessel bounds, dense-span testing, Bochner completeness/separability and the closed derivative graph then prove the unchanged statement.

Zero extension is an elementary isometry but was bundled into F5 as if supplied by the density lemma Statement. F5 now records only density; proof 1.2 proves measurability, equality of squared integrals and preservation of null-set equivalence directly. F7 now cites the actual separability definition. Closed weak-derivative graph, the relative countable-base construction, density and Poincaré establish the unchanged evolution triple.

On all of C(J,R^m), the original c(s) term varies with the argument, so the claimed contraction estimate fails even for B=0. The repaired Picard map uses a fixed incoming vector c_s, starting from u_h^0 and then previous endpoints. Finite concatenation gives existence and uniqueness with the required initial value; the bounded continuous solution vector, essentially bounded B and F∈L² give c′∈L², and energy testing gives the stated estimate.

The time-mollification Statement assumes ACω but does not establish its necessity for either approximation component. A1 now says assumed rather than required. Smooth energy testing gives the displayed uniform trace estimate; graph-norm approximants are uniformly H-Cauchy and the dual products converge in L¹, proving endpoint identities, real polarization and uniqueness of the continuous representative.

The proof used 1/n without restricting n≥1. Replacing it by 1/(n+1) defines the ACω density selection for every n∈N and preserves convergence. The space-time inf-sup estimate, right-kernel test w=ty, measurable inverse action, weak limit and bounded trace pass establish existence, initial trace and the full energy inequality; BNB gives uniqueness.

The complete cited published Poincaré proof establishes ||v||₂≤(b−a)||Dv||₂ in steps 2.1 and 3.1, explicitly obtaining C(p)=1. For the unit-width square this yields the exact alpha=1/2 with the full H¹ norm. Direct barycentric integration gives mass 1/6, stiffness 4, Ritz factor 2/3 and residual −q′/90 as claimed. The broader supplier Statement does not invalidate its explicit proved bound.
